name: Chelsea Manning
milestone_by_age_26: In early 2010, at age 22, as a U.S. Army intelligence analyst in Iraq, leaked nearly 750,000 classified military and diplomatic documents to WikiLeaks—the largest unauthorized disclosure of U.S. state secrets in history at the time—including the Collateral Murder video, Iraq/Afghan war logs, and diplomatic cables.
early_history_summary: Born Bradley Manning in Oklahoma City in December 1987 to a Navy veteran father and Welsh mother, Manning grew up largely unsupervised near Crescent, Oklahoma, and later in Wales after parents' divorce. A skilled early computer user who built a website at age 10, Manning enlisted in the U.S. Army in 2007, trained as an intelligence analyst with TS/SCI clearance, and deployed to Iraq in 2009 where access to SIPRNet enabled the 2010 leaks.
family_context_summary: Born to Susan Fox (Welsh) and Brian Manning (U.S. Navy intelligence analyst for five years); both parents struggled with alcoholism; chaotic childhood with periods of neglect near Crescent, Oklahoma, then Wales after divorce.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father had served as a U.S. Navy intelligence analyst and later worked as an IT manager; partial domain adjacency to intelligence work, though household was unstable rather than a structured apprenticeship.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Army intelligence access, SIPRNet, family instability, gender dysphoria under DADT, early computing
evidence_summary: Manning's material break was the 2010 WikiLeaks disclosures at age 22 while serving as an Army intelligence analyst in Iraq. Early life was marked by parental alcoholism, neglect, and moves between Oklahoma and Wales; father had prior Navy intelligence experience and later IT work. Manning's TS/SCI clearance and direct immersion in classified war data, combined with severe personal adversity, enabled a historically large leak rather than institutional pipeline advantages.
starting_point: Born December 1987 in Oklahoma City to a Navy veteran father and Welsh mother; grew up near Crescent, Oklahoma, then Haverfordwest, Wales, amid parental alcoholism and family instability.
current_position: American activist, security consultant, and public speaker living as a transgender woman; continues advocacy on transparency, privacy, and LGBTQ rights after 2017 sentence commutation.

trajectory.event: Enlisted in the U.S. Army and began intelligence analyst training with TS/SCI clearance.
Deployed to Forward Operating Base Hammer near Baghdad with access to SIPRNet and JWICS classified networks.
Leaked nearly 750,000 classified documents and videos to WikiLeaks; arrested in May 2010.
Court-martialed, convicted of Espionage Act and related charges, sentenced to 35 years; publicly came out as Chelsea.
President Obama commuted sentence; released after nearly seven years in custody.
Challenged Ben Cardin in Maryland Democratic Senate primary, receiving about 5.8% of the vote.
Jailed again for contempt for refusing to testify before a grand jury investigating Julian Assange; released in 2020.

name: Joe Lonsdale
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Palantir Technologies around 2003–2004 (company incorporated May 2003; prototype work 2004) with Peter Thiel, Alex Karp, Stephen Cohen, and Nathan Gettings while finishing Stanford CS—age ~21—building data analytics software for intelligence and defense.
early_history_summary: Raised in Fremont, California, in a competitive family (Irish Catholic father, Jewish mother). Studied computer science at Stanford (BS 2004), edited The Stanford Review (founded by Peter Thiel), interned at PayPal, then worked at Thiel's Clarium Capital before co-founding Palantir as a young Stanford-linked engineer.
family_context_summary: Grew up in Fremont, California, with two brothers; father Irish Catholic, mother Jewish; described family as very competitive. Specific parental occupations and wealth not detailed in reviewed sources.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources as tech or finance professionals; advantage appears more institutional (Stanford) and mentor-based (Thiel) than family-domain apprenticeship.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Stanford CS, Stanford Review, Peter Thiel mentor, PayPal/Clarium network, Bay Area
evidence_summary: Lonsdale co-founded Palantir at about age 21 after Stanford CS, PayPal internship, and Clarium Capital under Peter Thiel. Early path combined elite university access, libertarian student media network, and direct mentorship from Thiel rather than documented family wealth or domain inheritance. Subsequent companies (Addepar, OpenGov) and 8VC compounded that early Palantir stake and network.
starting_point: Born ~1982 in the Bay Area; raised in Fremont, California, in a competitive mixed Irish Catholic/Jewish household before attending Stanford.
current_position: Founder and managing partner of 8VC (Austin); serial founder of Palantir, Addepar, and OpenGov; active political donor and co-founder of University of Austin and Cicero Institute.

trajectory.event: Served as editor-in-chief of The Stanford Review while studying computer science at Stanford.
Co-founded Palantir Technologies with Thiel, Karp, Cohen, and Gettings after PayPal internship and Clarium work.
Left day-to-day Palantir role and co-founded Addepar, a wealth-management data platform.
Co-founded Formation 8 venture firm; later founded 8VC after Formation 8 dissolved.
Co-founded OpenGov government software company (later acquired by Cox Enterprises).
Relocated 8VC and family from Bay Area to Austin, Texas; Palantir went public.

name: Stephen Cohen
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Palantir Technologies in 2003 at age 20 (born September 30, 1982; company founded May 6, 2003) as a Stanford computer science student; credited with building the initial Palantir prototype in about eight weeks and remaining president and board member.
early_history_summary: Born September 30, 1982, in California (Ashkenazi Jewish descent). Studied computer science at Stanford with focus on ML, AI, and NLP, including research with Andrew Ng. Worked with Peter Thiel at Clarium Capital, then co-founded Palantir with Thiel, Karp, Lonsdale, and Gettings while finishing college.
family_context_summary: Of Ashkenazi Jewish descent, born in California; detailed parental occupations and finances not documented in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Stanford CS, Andrew Ng research, Thiel/Clarium, Palantir cofounders, post-9/11 intel wave
evidence_summary: Cohen co-founded Palantir at 20 as a Stanford CS student after Clarium Capital exposure under Thiel and research with Andrew Ng. He built the early prototype and has remained president/board member through IPO and beyond. Advantages center on Stanford technical training, Thiel network, and complementary cofounders rather than documented family capital.
starting_point: Born September 30, 1982, in California; Ashkenazi Jewish background; Stanford computer science path into Thiel's orbit.
current_position: Co-founder, president, and board member of publicly traded Palantir Technologies; substantial equity holder with large disclosed share sales in 2020–2025.

trajectory.event: Co-founded Palantir Technologies and built early prototype while finishing Stanford CS.
Joined Palantir board of directors; continued as core technical/executive founder.
Palantir IPO via direct listing; sold millions of shares around the public listing.
Executed large planned stock sales representing a significant fraction of remaining stake while remaining president.

name: Nathan Gettings
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Palantir Technologies on May 6, 2003, at age 26 (born March 1977) as a former PayPal engineer; with Thiel funding, built early prototype applying PayPal-style fraud detection techniques to intelligence analysis alongside Stanford students Lonsdale and Cohen.
early_history_summary: Former early PayPal engineer who brought production fraud-detection and engineering experience into the Palantir founding team. Public records (UK Companies House for Palantir Technologies UK; Florida resident records; Wikidata) place birth in March 1977; Illinois sources note a mathematics BA around 1998. Co-founded Palantir in 2003 and later held roles including at Affirm.
primary_early_advantage_tags: PayPal engineering, Thiel network, Palantir cofounders, post-9/11 analytics wave
evidence_summary: Gettings is consistently listed as a Palantir co-founder and early PayPal engineer who helped prototype the product in 2003–2004. Birth in March 1977 (Companies House and public records) puts him at 26 at the May 2003 founding. Family background is sparsely documented; leverage came from PayPal production experience and Thiel-linked team rather than public family platform.
starting_point: Born March 1977; early path ran through mathematics study and PayPal engineering before Palantir—family origin details not documented in reviewed sources.
current_position: Palantir co-founder; later founder/CRO roles including Affirm; lower public profile than fellow Palantir founders as of mid-2020s.

trajectory.event: Completed mathematics bachelor's degree (Illinois sources list BA '98) before tech industry roles.
Co-founded Palantir Technologies as former PayPal engineer building early intel analytics prototype.
Associated with continued Palantir technical leadership in early growth years before later external roles.
Later entrepreneurial and risk roles including RoboteX and subsequently Affirm risk leadership per public profiles.

name: Erik Finman
milestone_by_age_26: Became a self-made bitcoin millionaire by age 18 after investing a $1,000 grandmother gift into bitcoin at age 12 in 2011 (~$12/BTC), then compounding holdings; widely covered as a teenage crypto millionaire while still under 26.
early_history_summary: Grew up in Post Falls, Idaho. At 12, used $1,000 from his grandmother to buy bitcoin around May 2011 after striking a deal with parents to pursue an unconventional path instead of traditional college. Dropped out of high school, built a public persona around crypto investing and education startups, and was reported as a multi-millionaire by late teens.
family_context_summary: Grew up in Post Falls, Idaho; grandmother provided a $1,000 gift that seeded the bitcoin purchase; parents agreed to a deal allowing nontraditional education if he grew the capital to $1 million.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented as finance or tech professionals; parental support was permissiveness around education path rather than domain expertise.
primary_early_advantage_tags: early bitcoin buy, grandmother seed capital, parental education flexibility, media amplification
evidence_summary: Finman's qualifying arc is early bitcoin ownership at 12 and millionaire status by 18, repeatedly confirmed by Investopedia, Business Insider, and The Guardian. Advantages were modest seed capital, family flexibility on schooling, and riding the bitcoin structural wave rather than elite institutions or inherited networks. Later public profile exceeds enduring operator-scale impact relative to tier-1 founders.
starting_point: Born ~1998 and raised in Post Falls, Idaho; middle-American small-town upbringing with a grandmother gift and parental flexibility on schooling.
current_position: Crypto investor and entrepreneur known for early bitcoin wealth; continues public commentary on crypto and alternative education (profile primarily 2018–2019 peak media period).

trajectory.event: Invested ~$1,000 grandmother gift into bitcoin at about $12 per coin.
Reached self-reported millionaire status via crypto holdings; media branded him teenage bitcoin millionaire.
Widely profiled (Guardian, Investopedia) as high-school-dropout crypto entrepreneur.
Business Insider reported roughly $4.5M net worth from expanded bitcoin holdings.

name: Gavin Andresen
milestone_by_age_26: Bitcoin involvement began in 2010 (Bitcoin Faucet) and he became Bitcoin Core lead developer in 2011 at age ~44–45; no material, independently verified founder/engineering fame milestone at or before age 26 found (Princeton CS graduation 1988 at ~22 is ordinary educational completion, not the career-defining event).
early_history_summary: Born Gavin Bell on November 11, 1966, in Melbourne; moved to the U.S. at age five and grew up in Seattle, Anchorage, and California. Princeton CS graduate (1988); early career in 3D graphics/VR at Silicon Graphics. Discovered bitcoin in 2010 and was designated lead Bitcoin Core developer by Satoshi Nakamoto.
evidence_summary: Andresen's historically important work on Bitcoin Core and the Bitcoin Foundation occurred in his mid-40s. Early career graphics work after Princeton does not constitute a documented material public milestone by 26 under this project's strict age rule.

name: Hal Finney
milestone_by_age_26: Bitcoin first-transaction recipient and early mining (January 2009) occurred at age 52; reusable proof-of-work (2004) at ~48. Caltech EE BS in 1979 was age ~23 ordinary graduation. No material crypto/founder milestone by age 26 found.
early_history_summary: Born Harold Thomas Finney II on May 4, 1956, in Coalinga, California. Caltech electrical engineering graduate (1979). Early career included game development and later PGP Corporation cryptography with Phil Zimmermann. Became one of the first Bitcoin users and received the first BTC transaction from Satoshi in January 2009; died of ALS in 2014.
family_context_summary: Born to Virginia and Harold Thomas Finney in Coalinga, California; further family financial/domain detail not documented in reviewed sources.
evidence_summary: Finney is a foundational Bitcoin figure, but his defining milestones (RPOW 2004; first BTC transaction 2009) were in middle age. No age-≤26 material milestone meeting project criteria was identified.

name: Jesse Pollak
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Clef (passwordless authentication) around 2012–2013 at about age 22–23; ran the company for roughly five years before joining Coinbase via acquisition path in 2017, establishing early founder/operator track record well before creating Base in his 30s.
early_history_summary: Raised in Washington, D.C., attending a Quaker school for about 15 years. Encountered bitcoin around 2012; co-founded Clef with Mark Hudnall and Brennen Byrne to build passwordless identity. After Clef's wind-down/acquisition path, joined Coinbase engineering (~2017), scaled consumer engineering, then created Base L2 (public launch 2023).
family_context_summary: Grew up in Washington, D.C., with long Quaker schooling; family friend painted a tree mural in childhood bedroom (Fortune profile). Parental occupations not documented in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Clef founding, early crypto identity, Coinbase internal platform, Quaker education values
evidence_summary: Pollak's ≤26 milestone is co-founding Clef in the early 2010s (Wikipedia Clef: founded 2013; other bios say ~2012 and five-year run into 2017 Coinbase entry). Candidate birth year 1990 implies age ~23 at founding. Later Base success (2023) is larger but after 26; early founder reps and Coinbase consumer engineering formed the path.
starting_point: Raised in Washington, D.C., with long Quaker schooling; early adult entry into crypto identity startups rather than elite institutional pipelines documented.
current_position: Creator of Base and Head of Protocols / onchain efforts at Coinbase; leading executive voice for Coinbase's Ethereum L2 strategy.

trajectory.event: Encountered bitcoin and began building passwordless identity startup Clef with cofounders.
Clef founded (documented 2013); later raised seed capital and integrated with major sites.
Joined Coinbase engineering after Clef acquisition/wind-down path; began scaling consumer product engineering.
After leading large consumer engineering org, tasked by Brian Armstrong to bring Coinbase onchain.
Publicly launched Base, Coinbase's Ethereum layer-2 network, which became a top L2 by activity.

name: Balaji Srinivasan
milestone_by_age_26: Primary material milestone—co-founding Counsyl in 2007—occurred at age 27 (born May 24, 1980). Stanford degrees/teaching through mid-20s are educational, not the career-defining breakout; a16z GP, Coinbase CTO, and Network State fame came later. No clear material milestone at ≤26 established.
early_history_summary: Born May 24, 1980, on Long Island to physician parents who immigrated from Tamil Nadu, India. Earned BS/MS/PhD in electrical engineering plus MS in chemical engineering at Stanford; taught statistics/bioinformatics there. Co-founded Counsyl (2007), later a16z GP, Coinbase CTO via Earn.com acquisition, and author of The Network State.
family_context_summary: Son of physician parents who immigrated from Tamil Nadu, India; raised in Plainview, Long Island—professional immigrant household.
parent_family_domain_summary: Both parents physicians; medical/scientific household fluency, though Counsyl genomics is adjacent rather than direct clinical practice transfer.
evidence_summary: Despite strong early credentials, Counsyl founding at 27 falls outside the strict age-26 eligibility cutoff. Fame as investor, Coinbase CTO, and Network State author is later. Marked ineligible under project rules.

name: Chris Dixon
milestone_by_age_26: SiteAdvisor co-founding (2005) and McAfee sale (2006) occurred at about age 33–34 (born 1971/1972). Hunch (2009) and a16z partnership (2012) were later. No material founding milestone by age 26 found.
early_history_summary: Grew up in Ohio; studied philosophy at Columbia (after transferring from Wesleyan) and earned Harvard MBA. Early VC work at Bessemer; co-founded SiteAdvisor in 2005 (sold to McAfee 2006), then Hunch (sold to eBay 2011); joined Andreessen Horowitz in 2012 and became a leading crypto investor.
family_context_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources beyond Ohio upbringing.
evidence_summary: Dixon's breakout companies and a16z crypto platform leadership arrived in his 30s and beyond. No verified ≤26 material milestone under project criteria.

name: Ben Horowitz
milestone_by_age_26: Netscape product leadership began ~1995 (age ~29); Loudcloud/Opsware co-founding in 1999 at age 33; a16z founding in 2009 at age 43. No material founder/executive milestone by age 26 found.
early_history_summary: Born Benjamin Abraham Horowitz January 13, 1966, in London; son of writer David Horowitz. Worked at Lotus, then Netscape under Marc Andreessen, later AOL. Co-founded Loudcloud (Opsware) in 1999, sold to HP for $1.6B in 2007; co-founded Andreessen Horowitz in 2009.
family_context_summary: Son of David Horowitz, prominent writer/political figure; born in London. Family intellectual/political prominence documented; detailed early financial platform not fully scored here because person is ineligible.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father David Horowitz was a well-known author and activist—cultural/intellectual capital rather than software domain apprenticeship.
evidence_summary: Horowitz became a defining Silicon Valley CEO-operator and VC, but defining company founding (Loudcloud 1999) was at 33. Ineligible under age-26 rule.

name: Alfred Lin
milestone_by_age_26: In 1996, at about age 24, dropped out of a Stanford PhD program to join Tony Hsieh's LinkExchange as CFO; roughly 18 months later (~1997–1998, age ~25–26) LinkExchange sold to Microsoft for $265 million—material early operator/exit milestone by 26.
early_history_summary: Born 1972 in Taiwan; immigrated to New York at age six; attended Stuyvesant High School, Harvard (applied math BA), and Stanford (statistics MS). Met Tony Hsieh at Harvard via pizza arbitrage anecdote; joined LinkExchange as CFO, then co-founded Venture Frogs, later COO/CFO/chairman of Zappos through Amazon acquisition, then Sequoia partner (managing partner from 2025).
family_context_summary: Born in Taiwan; family immigrated to New York when he was six. Attended selective Stuyvesant High School—suggests high-achieving immigrant household; detailed parental occupations not documented.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources as tech operators; advantage appears educational selection rather than family business in internet commerce.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Tony Hsieh partnership, Harvard/Stanford, Stuyvesant, LinkExchange exit, immigrant high-achievement path
evidence_summary: Lin's age-26 window includes joining LinkExchange as CFO at ~24 and participating in the Microsoft acquisition for $265M by ~26. Later Zappos and Sequoia careers built on that Hsieh partnership and operator reputation. Early advantages: selective schools and an exceptional peer cofounder/partner rather than documented family capital.
starting_point: Born 1972 in Taiwan; moved to New York at age six; Stuyvesant → Harvard applied math → Stanford statistics path.
current_position: Managing partner of Sequoia Capital (appointed 2025 with Pat Grady); former Zappos COO/CFO/chairman and long-time Sequoia partner known for Airbnb and other consumer bets.

trajectory.event: Left Stanford PhD track to join LinkExchange as CFO with Tony Hsieh and cofounders.
LinkExchange sold to Microsoft for about $265 million after roughly 18 months.
Became chairman/COO/CFO of Zappos, scaling operations through first profitable years.
Amazon acquired Zappos for about $1.2 billion; Lin realized large personal and Venture Frogs gains.
Joined Sequoia Capital as partner after leaving Zappos.
Named managing partner of Sequoia Capital alongside Pat Grady.
